title: Credential-status query correlation budget and cache-partition privacy boundary
hypothesis: A synthetic status-query privacy contract can detect singleton and cross-context correlation risks in batching and cache partitioning while preserving accurate status semantics and making no live-service assurance claim.
null_or_failure: A singleton query exposes use timing, cache keys join unrelated holders, issuer and verifier contexts collapse, stale status is accepted, padding is treated as anonymity proof, revocation semantics change, or synthetic vectors become production privacy or exhaustive-security evidence.
test_falsifier_or_gate: Mutate singleton batching, timing buckets, cache partition, requester key, issuer boundary, stale age, suspension and revocation values, and production claims; require leakage cases to fail closed while live services remain zero.
rollback_or_recovery: Quarantine the unsafe query plan, retain the vector, restore the strictest context partition and freshness rule, and require real service measurement, privacy review, interoperability, and independent security review before production use.
boundary: Synthetic correlation vectors do not establish live-service privacy assurance, interoperability, or exhaustive security.
